properties.name: Howard Street between Rosslyn Street and William Street — bioretention bed
properties.popup_en: The City inventory classifies this asset as a bioretention bed. Raingardens filter runoff through vegetation and filter media; the marker does not indicate live performance or protection for nearby properties.
properties.location_note: Official garden-bed record coordinates; converted from EPSG:7855 to EPSG:4326 using Esri GeometryServer project. A point represents the garden-bed asset, not an inlet, exact polygon boundary or tree-pit identification.
properties.attribution: City of Melbourne; garden-bed survey supplied by Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria. Coordinates transformed and selected for this prototype research.
properties.scope_note: Within the prototype catchment polygon; this is not an independent verification of catchment boundaries or drainage connectivity.

properties.name: Lincoln Square stormwater harvesting and flood-mitigation system
properties.location_note: Official park landmark coordinate; NOT the underground tank coordinate.
properties.popup_en: Underground storage at Lincoln Square captures stormwater for park irrigation. The system can be emptied before heavy rain to provide space for incoming runoff and help limit downstream flooding. Current condition is unverified.
properties.attribution: City of Melbourne, landmark/street data; representative location selected for this prototype research. Project description sources linked separately.
properties.limitation: Historical/project evidence only; no current performance, maintenance, available storage or property-level protection is established.
properties.capacity_context: Published project capacity, not current available storage.
properties.license: CC BY 4.0 (coordinate data only; project descriptions are original paraphrases of linked sources)

properties.name: Queen Victoria Market rainwater harvesting system
properties.location_note: Representative point on Queen Street between Therry and Franklin, selected using the historic schematic. The documented tank was west of the street; this is NOT its surveyed position.
properties.popup_en: A documented rainwater system collects runoff from market shed roofs for toilet flushing, reducing drinking-water demand and runoff to the Elizabeth Street drainage system. The historic system included a 600 kL underground tank. Current condition is unverified.
properties.attribution: City of Melbourne, landmark/street data; representative location selected for this prototype research. Project description sources linked separately.
properties.limitation: Historical/project evidence only; no current performance, maintenance, available storage or property-level protection is established.
properties.capacity_context: capacity of the system documented in the 2013 case study, not a verified 2026 renewal capacity
properties.license: CC BY 4.0 (coordinate data only; project descriptions are original paraphrases of linked sources)
